content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Recognise and sketch the graphs of $y = \sin x$, $y = \cos x$, and $y = \tan x$
Identify the period, amplitude, and key features of each trigonometric graph
Understand the symmetry and periodicity of trigonometric functions
Use trigonometric graphs to find multiple solutions to equations

Trigonometric functions appear throughout science and engineering. Sound waves, light waves, tides, and even the motion of a Ferris wheel can all be modelled using sine and cosine curves. Understanding the shape and properties of these graphs is essential for solving trigonometric equations and modelling periodic phenomena.
of a trigonometric function is the horizontal length of one complete cycle before the graph repeats.
is the maximum distance from the centre line (the $x$-axis for standard trig graphs) to a peak or trough.
The sine graph starts at the origin, rises to a maximum of 1 at $90°$, returns to 0 at $180°$, drops to a minimum of $-1$ at $270°$, and returns to 0 at $360°$.
Rotational symmetry about the origin (odd function: $\sin(-x) = -\sin x$)
The cosine graph starts at its maximum of 1, drops to 0 at $90°$, reaches a minimum of $-1$ at $180°$, returns to 0 at $270°$, and rises back to 1 at $360°$.
Line symmetry about the $y$-axis (even function: $\cos(-x) = \cos x$)
The cosine graph is the same shape as the sine graph, but shifted $90°$ to the left. That is, $\cos x = \sin(x + 90°)$.
The tangent graph is fundamentally different from sine and cosine. It has no amplitude, and it has vertical asymptotes where the function is undefined.
$\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$, so $\tan x$ is undefined wherever $\cos x = 0$.
The sine and cosine graphs are closely related:
$$\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1 \quad \text{(for all values of } x\text{)}$$

When sketching trig graphs, always label key points: intercepts, maxima, minima, and asymptotes.
Remember that $\sin$ and $\cos$ are bounded between $-1$ and $1$, but $\tan$ has no bounds.
For solving equations, always check how many solutions are expected in the given range.
If you are asked to solve in radians, remember $360° = 2\pi$ and $180° = \pi$.
Sketch the graph if you are unsure about which solutions to include.
$y = \sin x$ starts at 0, has period $360°$, amplitude 1, and is an odd function
$y = \cos x$ starts at 1, has period $360°$, amplitude 1, and is an even function
$y = \tan x$ starts at 0, has period $180°$, no amplitude, and has asymptotes at odd multiples of $90°$
$\cos x = \sin(x + 90°)$ -- cosine is a shifted sine curve
